newsitem.title: UK: Russia talk persists in minor metals.
newsitem.headline: Russia talk persists in minor metals.

text.p: Talk of the possible movement to the market of material from Russian stockpiles of strategic metals continued to reverberate in the market on Wednesday, European traders said.
Several said they were sure that Russian reserves had started to enter and stir the market.

Recently traders said they believed that 420 tonnes of cobalt, 30,000 76 lb flasks of mercury, 7,000 tonnes of titanium sponge and an undisclosed amount of chrome could be released from strategic stockpiles.
On cobalt, one trader said that most of the metal had entered the market but believed that it had found buyers from consumers to cover their commitments.
Cobalt has the potential to withstand new supply but one trader suggested that further sales from Russia will be seen near-term.
"There are additional amounts of Russian cobalt in the pipeline," one European trader said. "Negotiations are in place from Russian reserves."
"The move by the Russians has helped to dent sentiment in cobalt but still metal on the ground remains tight," a trade source said.

Some traders think Russia will now revive a policy of selling strategic stockpiles and that the government has a specific amount to sell, so that the rumoured 420 tonnes was the first stage in their programme.
On Tuesday trade sources said that a large proportion of the cobalt had already sold to a major trade organisation.
Russian authorities would not comment on the recent.
